prompt: Which module system does this course write new code in?

choices.why: Right: the language's own, shared with browsers.

choices.text: CommonJS, because most of npm uses it
choices.why: You depend on it; you do not have to write it.
A project picks one with `type`, and this course picks modules.
Only lesson 3 uses both, to compare them.

prompt: Why can a `require` sit inside an `if`, while an `import` statement cannot?

choices.text: `require` is a call made while the file runs
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `import` is slower, so it has to be at the top
choices.why: Speed is not the reason; timing is.
It can contain most statements; `import` declarations are the exception.
It is Node's; browsers never had it.

prompt: A file is called `report.cjs`, in a folder whose `package.json` says `"type": "module"`. What is it?

choices.why: Right. The extension wins.
`type` only decides for plain `.js` files.
Detection is only for a `.js` with no package.json.

choices.text: Neither: Node refuses to load it
choices.why: `.cjs` is loaded wherever it is.

prompt: `hello.js` uses `import` and sits beside `{ "name": "typeless" }`. It ran and printed a warning. What did the warning say to do?

choices.why: That would make it CommonJS, and its `import` would fail.
Right: the last line of the warning.
That would bring back detection, not fix the project.
No flag is needed for ES modules in Node 22.

prompt: A project says `"type": "module"`, and a tool insists on loading its configuration file with `require`. What is the least disruptive fix?

choices.text: Change the whole project to CommonJS
choices.why: One file needs to differ, not all of them.

choices.text: Remove `type` and let Node detect each file
choices.why: Detection reparses and warns, and only works with no package.json.
Right. That is what the extension is for.
The tool would still `require` its own file name.

prompt: `require("express")`: where does Node look first?

choices.why: That is the last place.
`express` is not built in, so the search goes on to node_modules.

choices.text: In `node_modules` beside the file that asks
choices.why: Right, then each parent folder.
Node never downloads anything; npm does, beforehand.

prompt: A package you never installed in a project is found anyway. What is the likeliest cause?

choices.text: Node caches packages from earlier projects
choices.why: The module cache lives inside one process only.

choices.text: A `node_modules` in a parent folder, such as your home
choices.why: Right. The search walks up to `/`.

choices.text: npm installed it globally by default
choices.why: npm installs into the project unless told `-g`, and `require` does not search the global folder.

choices.text: The package is built into Node
choices.why: Then it would have a `node:` name.

prompt: `import x from "./lib"` fails with `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT`, and `require("./lib")` worked. What do you write instead?

choices.why: Right: the whole path, as the error suggested.
Without `./` it becomes a package name.
A trailing slash still names a folder.
That failed too: no extension.

prompt: Match each specifier to how Node reads it.

pairs.right: a package, searched for in node_modules

right_distractors: a package downloaded on first use

prompt: Where do `require` and `__dirname` come from in a CommonJS file?

choices.why: They are not on `globalThis`.
Right. `module.wrapper` shows it.

choices.text: npm adds them when it installs a package
choices.why: They exist in files npm never touched.
package.json declares nothing like them.

prompt: `trap.js` contains `exports = { hello }` and nothing else. What does `require("./trap.js")` return?

choices.why: Only the parameter was pointed at a new object.
Right: module.exports, untouched.
require returns module.exports, which starts as an object.
Assigning to a parameter is allowed; it just does nothing useful.

prompt: A server opens `"./data.json"` and works when started from its folder, but fails under a process manager. What should the path be built from?

choices.why: That is the folder it was started from, which is the problem.
PATH is where commands are found, not files.
Right: the folder the file is in.
The service may run as a different user, and the file is beside the code.

prompt: Two files `require("./counter")`. How many times does `counter.js` run?

choices.why: It printed `counter.js runs` once.
next() runs a function inside it, not the file.
Right. The second gets the cached exports.
It ran at the first require.

prompt: A configuration object exported by `config.js` seems to reset itself in one part of the application. What is the likeliest cause?

choices.text: The cache expires after a minute
choices.why: It does not expire while the process runs.

choices.text: The module was loaded from two different paths
choices.why: Right. The cache is keyed by path.
They are, in a separate cache.

choices.text: Objects cannot be shared between files
choices.why: They can; that is what a singleton module does.

prompt: In the cycle, why did `b.js` see `a.ready` as `false`?

choices.why: Nothing failed; both printed.

choices.text: Booleans are copied, and copies never change
choices.why: It read the property of a shared object, too early.
a.js started first and required b.js on its second line.

choices.text: It received `a.js` half run, from the cache
choices.why: Right. A cycle hands over an unfinished module.

prompt: `start.mjs` prints a line, then imports a file that does not exist. What appears?

choices.why: The import is resolved before any code runs.

choices.text: The line, and an undefined value
choices.why: A missing module is an error, not a missing value.
Node printed ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
Right. `starting the server` never printed.

prompt: What does a top-level `await` in `prices.mjs` do to the modules that import it?

choices.text: They run in parallel with it
choices.why: Nothing runs in parallel; they wait.

choices.text: They receive a promise instead of `prices`
choices.why: They receive the finished value.
Top-level await is allowed in ES modules.

choices.text: They wait until it has finished
choices.why: Right.

prompt: An ES module imports a data file by adding `with { type: "___" }` after its name.
An ES module does `import pkg from "./slug.cjs"`. What is `pkg`?

choices.text: Only the first function in the file
choices.why: It is everything module.exports held.
Only `import()`, the function, returns a promise.
Right.

choices.text: `undefined`, as CommonJS has no default export
choices.why: The default import of CommonJS is module.exports.

prompt: `require("./later.mjs")` failed with `ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE`. What still works from CommonJS?

choices.why: The await is still there, whatever the name.
Right. import() works in both systems.
One form can.
require takes no options.

prompt: `import { format } from "old-lib"` says there is no export named `format`, but the library's documentation calls `lib.format()`. What do you try?

choices.why: The scan is the same idea in every version.

choices.text: Edit the library's own file inside node_modules
choices.why: The next install undoes it.

choices.text: Take the default import and call the method on it
choices.why: Right. Named imports from CommonJS are a guess from its text.
require is not defined in ES module scope.

prompt: `require("tidy/src/internal.js")` failed with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`, though the file exists. Why?

choices.why: The CommonJS build was loaded fine by name.

choices.text: The package's `exports` does not list it
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Files under `src` can never be loaded
choices.why: The folder name means nothing to Node.

choices.text: npm marked it private when installing
choices.why: npm did not install this package; you made it.

prompt: Why did `require("tidy")` and `import ... from "tidy"` load different files?

choices.text: Node picks a file at random
choices.why: It is decided by the conditions, every time.

choices.text: Each condition names its own file
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The second was cached from the first
choices.why: They were two separate processes.
There is no `main` in this package.json.

prompt: In a project's `imports` field, every name must start with the character ___.
Why write `node:fs` instead of `fs`?

choices.text: `fs` without the prefix was removed in Node 22
choices.why: It still works; the prefix is about certainty.

choices.text: So that no package ever stands in for it
choices.why: Right, and it says at a glance that the module is Node's.
Speed is not the reason.
It is optional for most modules in both systems.

prompt: How many names did `builtinModules` list in Node 22.22.0?
`require("test")` failed with `Cannot find module 'test'`, and `require("node:test")` worked. Why?

choices.text: The test runner only works in ES modules
choices.why: It loaded in CommonJS with the prefix.

choices.text: It needs to be installed with npm first
choices.why: It is built in; the prefix is what names it.
It loaded node:test fine.
Right. Without it, `test` is a package name.

prompt: Why does the links project keep `app.js` and `server.js` apart?

choices.why: Express is happy with one.
One file or two makes no difference to speed here.

choices.text: Because one is CommonJS and the other an ES module
choices.why: Both are ES modules.
Right. A test imports the application and starts it on a port the system picks; lesson 6 does exactly that.

prompt: Lesson 8 moves the links from an array to a file. Which files have to change, if the layout is followed?

choices.why: Right. That is why it exists.

choices.text: Every route that reads or writes a link
choices.why: Routes call the store, and never know where data lives.
Neither touches the data.
package.json does not list data files.

prompt: A CommonJS file calls `require("tidy")`. Put Node's steps in order.
items: See that `tidy` is not built in and is not a path
Look in `node_modules` beside the file, then in each parent
Read the package's `exports` for the `require` condition
Run that file, unless it is already in the cache
